다음 글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 어법상 알맞은 말로 바르게 연결된 것은?

After the map (A)[posted / was posted] online, something unexpected happened. The trees started receiving thousands of emails, but many of them were not reports about damage or poor health. Instead, they were love letters, poems, greetings, and messages (B)[expressing / expressed] appreciation for the trees. The tree mail phenomenon quickly spread, and people all over the world started sending messages.
…
The global popularity of the tree mail phenomenon (C)[remind / reminds] us that we are all connected to nature, and we are all involved in building a more sustainable world.

(A) - (B) - (C)
solution: (A)는 지도가 온라인에 '게시된' 것이므로 수동태 was posted가 맞다. (B)는 메시지가 감사를 '표현하는' 능동 관계이고 뒤에 목적어 appreciation이 있으므로 현재분사 expressing이 맞다. (C)의 주어는 The global popularity이며 of the tree mail phenomenon은 수식어구이므로 단수동사 reminds가 맞다. 따라서 정답은 ④이다.

body:
다음 글의 핵심 내용으로 가장 적절한 것은?

Moving a mouse can be difficult for people whose hand movements are limited. Accessible websites give these users another way to move around a page: a keyboard. Users can reach links, select buttons, and enter information into fields with keys. For instance, pressing the tab key moves them between different parts of a page. This feature also helps people who have temporarily injured a hand. By allowing keyboard navigation, websites make their content easier to access for people who have difficulty using a mouse.
solution: 글은 마우스 사용이 어려운 사람들이 키보드로 웹사이트의 링크, 버튼, 입력란에 접근할 수 있다고 설명한다. 따라서 키보드 탐색이 마우스 사용에 어려움이 있는 사람들의 웹사이트 이용을 돕는다는 ②가 핵심 내용이다.
choices: Learning keyboard shortcuts helps people write documents faster.
Keyboard navigation makes websites usable for people who struggle to use a mouse.
People with injured hands should avoid entering information online.
Websites should explain how a mouse and a keyboard work together.
Using a mouse is the easiest way for all users to explore websites.

body:
다음 글에 제목을 붙일 때 가장 적절한 것은?

Not everyone can get information by listening. Some website users have hearing disabilities, and others cannot play audio in a quiet library. Written forms of audio information can help both groups. A transcript presents the full audio content as text. Captions show text while a video plays and can describe music and other sounds as well as speech. These features allow users to understand audio information even when listening is difficult or impossible.
solution: 청각 장애가 있거나 소리를 재생할 수 없는 상황에서도 대본과 자막을 통해 음성 정보에 접근할 수 있다는 내용이다. 두 기능을 함께 포괄하는 제목은 음성 정보를 글로 제공하는 것을 다룬 ④이다.
choices: Finding Quiet Places to Watch Videos
Why Speech Matters More Than Other Sounds
Providing Written Access to Audio Information
Choosing Better Background Music for Websites

body:
다음 글 전체의 주제를 가장 잘 나타낸 것은?

A website may contain an image that provides information readers need to understand its text. For someone with a visual disability, however, that information may be difficult to access. A screen reader reads written content aloud, but it cannot explain an image on its own. Accessible websites therefore attach a short written description, called alt text, to the image. If students appear in a picture, the description can state their number and explain their actions. The screen reader can then read this description aloud. The important point is that information presented visually becomes available in a form the program can read.
solution: 이미지의 정보에 접근하기 어려운 문제를 대체 텍스트와 화면 낭독 프로그램이 함께 해결하는 과정이 중심이다. 따라서 시각 정보를 이용할 수 있도록 돕는 이미지 설명의 역할을 제시한 ①이 적절하다. ②는 모든 이미지를 글로 교체한다는 내용이므로 지문의 취지와 다르다.
choices: The role of image descriptions in making visual information accessible
The advantages of replacing all website images with written passages
The importance of selecting attractive pictures for online readers
The development of programs that recognize images without descriptions
The reasons students prefer spoken explanations to written information

body:
다음 글을 아우르는 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?

Making information available on a website does not always make it easy to use. People with poor eyesight may still find written content difficult to read. A clear difference between the colors of the text and its background can make the writing easier to see. Sound presents another issue. Accessible websites let users lower the volume of background sound or switch it off, giving them control over their listening experience. These features respond to different needs: one makes text clearer, while the other lets users manage sound. Their value is not limited to people who cannot see or hear at all.
solution: 글은 글자와 배경의 색 대비를 통한 가독성 개선과 배경음 조절 기능을 함께 설명한다. 따라서 서로 다른 이용상의 필요를 충족하는 두 기능을 모두 포괄한 ⑤가 적절하다. ②는 배경음의 전면 제거로 내용을 왜곡하고, ③은 글자 가독성만으로 접근성 문제 전체를 해결한다고 과장한다.
choices: Replacing Visual Content with Sound for Users with Poor Eyesight
Improving Web Accessibility by Removing Every Background Sound
Clearer Text: The Complete Solution to Website Accessibility
Why Websites Should Offer the Same Sensory Settings to Everyone
Clearer Text and Adjustable Sound: Meeting Different Access Needs

body:
다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하려고 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

Web accessibility involves more than placing information where people can find it. The form in which it is offered and the way users reach it also matter. An image may carry important information, but a screen reader needs a written description to communicate that information aloud. Audio content can be provided through transcripts or captions for people who cannot hear it. Likewise, links and buttons need to be reachable by keyboard for users who cannot easily operate a mouse. These features address different barriers, yet they share a purpose: enabling access to website information and functions through another means. Their usefulness also reaches beyond lasting disabilities. Captions help someone who cannot play sound in a quiet library, and keyboard navigation can help someone whose hand is temporarily injured. Thus, an accessibility feature designed to address one difficulty can also serve users facing a similar barrier for a different reason.

[요약문]
Web accessibility responds to barriers by (A) the ways users receive information or operate a site, and the value of these features is determined by users’ (B), rather than solely by whether they have lasting disabilities.
solution: 대체 텍스트, 대본·자막, 키보드 탐색은 정보 수용이나 사이트 조작 방식을 다양화하므로 (A)에는 diversifying이 적절하다. 또한 도서관 이용자와 일시적으로 손을 다친 사람의 사례는 영구적 장애 여부보다 실제 접근상의 필요가 중요함을 보여 주므로 (B)에는 access needs가 들어간다. 따라서 두 논점을 모두 반영한 정답은 ③이다.

body:
윗글을 읽고 답할 수 없는 질문은?

Did you know that there are over 7,000 languages currently being used around the world? Most of these languages are spoken by very small groups of people, and half of them could disappear within the next generation. This would be a great loss because language plays a big role in connecting people's identity to their culture. This is the reason why some organizations work to preserve them. For example, a nonprofit organization called Wikitongues has set the goal of preserving all languages that are in danger of being lost. The organization works to achieve this by recording videos of individuals speaking these languages and making mother-tongue resources more accessible.
solution: 지문은 사용 언어 수가 7,000개가 넘는다고 했고(①), 언어가 정체성과 문화를 이어 주기에 소멸이 큰 손실이라고 밝혔으며(②), Wikitongues의 목표(④)와 그 달성 방법(⑤, 영상 기록·모국어 자료 접근성 확대)을 설명한다. 그러나 Wikitongues가 언제 설립되었는지는 언급이 없으므로 답할 수 없는 질문은 ③이다.
choices: How many languages are currently used around the world?
Why would the loss of a language be a great loss?
When was the nonprofit organization Wikitongues founded?
What goal has Wikitongues set for itself?
How does Wikitongues work to preserve endangered languages?

body:
윗글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?

Singapore is known for its cultural diversity, and a good example of this is its hawker centers. At hawker centers, people from different ethnic backgrounds gather to enjoy delicious meals. Just like the people, the food reflects the wide range of diversity within Singapore, as food traditions from China, Malaysia, India, and other countries are passed down. In fact, hawker culture is an essential part of Singapore's cultural heritage. With over 110 hawker centers spread across the city, you won't have any trouble finding one, and the best part is that the food prices are affordable.
solution: 지문은 싱가포르 전역에 110개가 넘는(over 110) 호커 센터가 있다고 했다. 따라서 100개 미만이라는 ④는 지문과 일치하지 않는다. ①은 첫 문장(known for its cultural diversity), ②는 둘째 문장(people from different ethnic backgrounds gather), ③은 셋째 문장(the food reflects the wide range of diversity), ⑤는 마지막 문장(the food prices are affordable)과 각각 일치한다.
choices: Singapore is famous for its cultural diversity.
At hawker centers, people from various ethnic backgrounds eat together.
The food sold at hawker centers reflects Singapore's diversity.
There are fewer than 100 hawker centers across Singapore.
The food prices at hawker centers are affordable.

body:
윗글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?

During World War II, there was a group of people who risked everything to protect invaluable works of art from destruction. In 1943, around 345 people from 14 different Allied nations came together to form the Monuments, Fine Arts, and Archives (MFAA) program. They were not trained soldiers but scholars and experts of various kinds, such as professors, historians, and architects. These brave men and women volunteered to protect Europe's cultural heritage and became known as the "Monuments Men."
solution: 지문은 MFAA 구성원들이 훈련받은 군인이 아니라 교수·역사학자·건축가 같은 학자와 전문가였다고 밝힌다(They were not trained soldiers but scholars and experts). 따라서 대부분이 훈련받은 군인이었다는 ③은 지문과 일치하지 않는다. 설립 연도 1943년(①), 14개 연합국에서 온 약 345명(②), 구성원의 직업(④), 'Monuments Men'이라는 별칭(⑤)은 모두 지문과 일치한다.
choices: The MFAA program was formed in 1943.
About 345 people from 14 Allied nations came together to create the MFAA.
Most members of the MFAA were professionally trained soldiers.
The members of the MFAA included professors, historians, and architects.
The members of the MFAA came to be called the "Monuments Men."

body:
윗글의 내용을 바르게 이해한 학생끼리 짝지은 것은?

One of the largest collections of stolen items was hidden in the salt mines of Altaussee, Austria. Upon discovering its location, some of the Monuments Men rushed to the mines, hoping to recover everything before it was too late. Meanwhile, the Nazi leader who was in charge of the area tried to destroy everything by setting off large explosives inside the mines. Luckily, some local miners found the explosives and came up with a plan to protect their livelihood. They secretly removed the large explosives and put smaller ones at the entrances. Once they went off, the Nazi leader believed that everything was destroyed. However, while the small explosions sealed off the entrances, they left the rest of the mines and the works of art unharmed. When the Monuments Men arrived and squeezed their way into the mines, they were amazed to see thousands of priceless objects, including paintings, statues, books, furniture, and more.

• 민준: A huge collection of stolen items was kept in salt mines in Austria.
• 서연: The local miners' main purpose was to save the works of art from the Nazis.
• 지우: The small explosions blocked the entrances but did not damage the artworks inside.
• 하은: The Nazi leader realized that the artworks had survived the explosions.
• 준서: The Monuments Men entered the mines easily because the entrances were open.
solution: 민준: 첫 문장에서 대규모 장물이 오스트리아 Altaussee의 소금 광산에 숨겨져 있었다고 했으므로 맞다. 서연: 광부들이 계획을 세운 목적은 '자신들의 생계를 지키는 것(to protect their livelihood)'이었다. 작품을 지키는 것이 주된 목적이었다고 볼 근거는 없으므로 틀리다. 지우: 작은 폭발이 입구만 막았고 광산의 나머지 부분과 작품은 손상되지 않았다(sealed off the entrances, ... left the rest of the mines and the works of art unharmed)고 했으므로 맞다. 하은: 나치 지도자는 모든 것이 파괴되었다고 믿었으므로(believed that everything was destroyed) 틀리다. 준서: 입구가 폭발로 막혀 Monuments Men이 비집고 들어갔다(squeezed their way into the mines)고 했으므로, 입구가 열려 있어 쉽게 들어갔다는 말은 틀리다. 따라서 바르게 이해한 학생은 민준과 지우이고 정답은 ②이다.

body:
다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~⑤ 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?

“To grow into a better version of ourselves, we should not stay as we are.” That was the first thing our teacher said to us on the first day of school. She wanted us ①starting the semester by ②pushing ourselves out of our comfort zones and learning more about ourselves. To help us ③do so, she gave us an assignment to challenge ourselves in three different ways. The three challenges could involve hobbies, exercise, our studies, or even our relationships. The important part was ④trying something new for each one. She told us that we should ⑤share our experiences with our classmates when we finished the challenges.
solution: want는 목적어 뒤에 목적격 보어로 to부정사를 쓰므로 ①은 to start로 고쳐야 한다. ② 전치사 by 뒤에는 동명사 pushing이 온다. ③ help는 목적격 보어로 동사원형을 쓸 수 있으므로 do가 맞다. ④ be동사 뒤 보어 자리의 동명사 trying, ⑤ 조동사 should 뒤의 동사원형 share는 모두 어법상 맞다.

body:
다음 글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 어법상 알맞은 말로 바르게 연결된 것은?

These days, I tend (A)(watching / to watch) movies on streaming services. However, if I go to the theater, I usually watch an action or science fiction movie with my friends or family. Those are the kinds of movies they enjoy.
(중략)
At first, it felt a bit awkward and lonely to sit in the theater by myself. But once the movie started, I became completely (B)(absorbing / absorbed) in the story. It was so (C)(satisfying / satisfied) just to focus on the movie itself. There was nothing to distract me!

(A) — (B) — (C)
solution: (A) tend는 to부정사를 목적어로 써서 ‘~하는 경향이 있다’는 뜻이 되므로 to watch가 알맞다. (B) 주어 I가 이야기에 ‘몰두하게 된’ 것이므로 과거분사 absorbed를 쓴다. (C) 가주어 It이 가리키는 영화에 집중하는 것이 ‘만족감을 주는’ 것이므로 현재분사 satisfying이 알맞다.

body:
다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~⑤ 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?

Ever since I was a child, I’ve always been afraid of water. So I have never enjoyed water activities or felt comfortable while ①doing them. For the second challenge, I decided to try ②to overcome this discomfort.
However, I wasn’t sure what to do at first. One day, I came across a video clip of my cousin ③surfing at an indoor pool on social media. It looked fun, and I liked the fact ④that it took place in a shallow pool, not in the ocean. I messaged my cousin about it. She assured me that it wasn’t too hard, so I signed up for a beginner course.
At the beginning of the lesson, it was hard just to stand up on the board. After some help from the instructor, however, I learned how to balance properly and even managed ⑤surfing a few waves!
solution: manage는 to부정사를 목적어로 취해 '간신히 ~해내다'라는 뜻을 나타내므로 ⑤ surfing은 to surf로 고쳐야 한다. ① 접속사 while 뒤에서 주어와 be동사가 생략된 형태로, 현재분사 doing이 알맞다. ② 'try+to부정사'는 '~하려고 노력하다'라는 뜻으로, 두려움을 극복하려고 애쓴다는 문맥에 맞다. ③ 현재분사 surfing이 뒤에서 my cousin을 꾸며 '실내 수영장에서 서핑하는 사촌'이라는 뜻을 나타낸다. ④ that은 the fact의 내용을 설명하는 동격의 접속사로, 뒤에 완전한 절이 온다.

body:
다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 어법상 알맞은 것은?

Did you know that there are over 7,000 languages currently being used around the world? Most of these languages __________ by very small groups of people, and half of them could disappear within the next generation.
solution: 주어 Most of these languages는 사람들에 의해 '사용되는' 대상이므로 수동태가 와야 합니다. 뒤에 행위자를 나타내는 by very small groups of people이 있는 것도 단서가 됩니다. 주어 languages가 복수이므로 are spoken이 알맞습니다. ②~⑤는 모두 능동태여서 언어가 직접 말한다는 뜻이 되므로 틀립니다.

body:
다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 어법상 알맞은 것은?

When Germany began to lose the war, the stolen objects came under threat. Hitler ordered his forces __________ everything that could be useful to the Allied armies before they retreated from an area.
solution: order는 「order + 목적어 + to부정사」 형태로 쓰여 '~에게 …하라고 명령하다'라는 뜻을 나타냅니다. 따라서 목적격 보어 자리에는 to destroy가 와야 합니다. 동사원형, 동명사, 과거분사, 「of+동명사」는 order의 목적격 보어로 쓸 수 없습니다.

body: 다음 중 [ ] 안의 부분이 어법상 틀린 것은?
solution: 「leave + 목적어 + 목적격 보어」 구문에서 목적격 보어 자리에는 부사가 아니라 형용사(분사)가 옵니다. 따라서 unharmedly는 unharmed로 고쳐야 합니다. ①은 hope to 뒤의 동사원형, ②는 과거의 일에 대한 가능성을 나타내는 could have p.p., ③은 복수명사 explosives를 받는 ones, ⑤는 「be worth -ing」 구문이므로 모두 맞습니다.
choices: They hoped to [recover] everything before it was too late.
They secretly removed the large explosives and put smaller [ones] at the entrances.
The small explosions left the rest of the mines and the works of art [unharmedly].
It is worth [remembering] the Monuments Men's contribution to the preservation of cultural heritage.

body:
다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)의 각 괄호 안에서 어법상 알맞은 말로 바르게 짝지은 것은?

When the MFAA was first formed, its main goal was to prevent the destruction of cultural landmarks. The Monuments Men persuaded the Allied forces (A)[not to bomb / not bombing] areas with museums, churches, or other culturally significant buildings. They also visited areas that (B)[have / had] already been destroyed to restore (C)[damaged / damaging] architecture and works of art.

(A) – (B) – (C)
solution: (A) persuade는 「persuade + 목적어 + to부정사」 형태로 쓰고, to부정사를 부정할 때는 not을 to 앞에 두므로 not to bomb가 알맞습니다. (B) 지역들이 파괴된 것은 Monuments Men이 그곳을 방문한(visited) 과거 시점보다 먼저 일어난 일이므로 과거완료 had been destroyed를 써야 합니다. (C) 건축물은 '손상된' 대상이므로 수동의 의미를 나타내는 과거분사 damaged가 알맞습니다.

body:
다음 글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓕ 중 어법상 어색한 것을 모두 고른 것은?

One of the largest collections of stolen items ⓐwas hidden in the salt mines of Altaussee, Austria. Upon ⓑdiscover its location, some of the Monuments Men rushed to the mines. They hoped to recover everything before it was too late.
Meanwhile, the Nazi leader ⓒwho was in charge of the area tried to destroy everything by setting off large explosives inside the mines. This could have been disastrous. Luckily, some local miners found the explosives in the mines and came up with a plan to protect their livelihood. They secretly removed the large explosives and put smaller ones at the entrances. Once they went off, the Nazi leader believed ⓓwhat everything was destroyed. However, while the small explosions sealed off the entrances, they left the rest of the mines and the works of art ⓔunharmed.
When the Monuments Men arrived and squeezed their way into the mines, they must have been ⓕamazing to see what was inside.
solution: ⓑ 전치사 Upon 뒤에는 동명사가 와야 하므로 discovering으로 고쳐야 합니다. ⓓ believed 뒤에 완전한 절(everything was destroyed)이 이어지므로 명사절 접속사 that이 와야 합니다. ⓕ 사람이 '놀란' 감정을 느낀 것이므로 amazed로 고쳐야 합니다. 함정에 주의해야 합니다. ⓐ는 주어의 중심이 One이라서 단수 동사 was가 맞고, ⓔ는 leave의 목적격 보어로 쓰인 형용사(분사) unharmed라서 맞습니다.

body:
다음 글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ를 어법상 고쳐 쓴 것으로 알맞지 않은 것은?

The efforts of the Monuments Men did not end with the war. For several years, they continued the work of recovering cultural treasures and identifying where they ⓐhave been stolen from. In the end, the Monuments Men returned more than five million works of art and objects of cultural importance to their places of origin.
Not everything ⓑwhat was stolen by the Nazis has been found, but what the Monuments Men accomplished ⓒare truly amazing. Without this determined group, the search for stolen works of art might never ⓓhave begun. In addition, countless historical and cultural landmarks would have been lost forever due to the destruction of war. Thanks to their efforts, many incredible cultural sites and works of art have survived and can still ⓔappreciate to this day.
solution: ⓓ는 과거 사실과 반대되는 상황을 가정하는 「might + have p.p.」 형태이므로 원래 문장이 맞고, begin으로 고치면 오히려 틀립니다. ⓐ 보물이 도난당한 것은 그것을 찾아낸 과거 시점보다 먼저이므로 had가 맞습니다. ⓑ 선행사 everything이 있으므로 관계대명사 that이 와야 합니다. ⓒ what절이 주어이면 단수 취급하므로 is가 맞습니다. ⓔ 문화유산은 '감상되는' 대상이므로 수동태 be appreciated가 맞습니다.

body:
다음 글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 어법상 알맞은 말로 바르게 연결된 것은?

Grandma Moyo has been (A)[volunteering / volunteered] for the program for about eight years. She wanted to help people (B)[heal / healed] their wounded hearts. The grandmothers are also very reliable, which (C)[is / are] important for the program's efforts to support mental health.
solution: (A) 그녀가 스스로 자원봉사를 '하고 있는' 능동이므로 현재완료진행 have been volunteering의 volunteering이 맞습니다. (B) 「help+목적어+동사원형」 구조이므로 heal입니다. (C) which는 앞 절 전체(그들이 믿음직하다는 사실)를 받는 단수 취급이므로 is가 맞습니다. 따라서 ①입니다.

body:
다음 글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 어법상 알맞은 말로 바르게 연결된 것은?

The sessions are free and (A)[provide / are provided] by respected elderly women. These women, (B)[called / calling] "grandmothers," sit with patients and listen to their stories. Offering online counseling through an app has helped the program (C)[reach / to reaching] even more people.
solution: (A) 상담 시간이 '제공되는' 것이므로 수동태 are provided가 맞습니다. (B) women이 '불리는' 것이므로 과거분사 called입니다. (C) 「help+목적어+동사원형(또는 to부정사)」 구조인데 to reaching은 불가능하므로 reach가 맞습니다. 따라서 ②입니다.
choices: ④ are provided - called - to reaching

body:
다음 글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓕ 중, 어법상 어색한 것을 세 개 찾아 기호를 쓰고 알맞게 고쳐 쓰시오. (단, 다른 단어를 추가하지 말 것)

Dr. Chibanda: The idea came from an experience ⓐwhat I had as a psychiatrist. One of my patients ⓑhad become severely depressed. However, she couldn't get help because she was unable ⓒaffording the bus ride to the hospital. ⓓIn fact, it is difficult for many people in Zimbabwe to pay for transportation. Furthermore, there ⓔhas been a lack of psychiatrists in the country for many years. When the program started in 2006, there were only eleven psychiatrists ⓕserved Zimbabwe's population of over twelve million people.

기호 알맞게 고친 표현 (1) ____ : ____ (2) ____ : ____ (3) ____ : ____
solution: ⓐ 선행사 experience를 받는 목적격 관계대명사가 필요하므로 what이 아니라 which(또는 that)로 고칩니다. ⓒ 「be unable to+동사원형」이므로 affording을 to afford로 고칩니다. ⓕ 앞의 psychiatrists를 꾸미는 분사가 와야 하므로(동사 served로는 문장이 성립하지 않음) serving으로 고칩니다. ⓑ 과거완료, ⓓ 부사구, ⓔ 현재완료는 모두 올바릅니다.

body:
다음 글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중, 어법상 어색한 것을 두 개 찾아 기호를 쓰고 알맞게 고쳐 쓰시오. (단, 다른 단어를 추가하지 말 것)

Grandma Moyo: ⓐSeeking help for mental health problems is nothing to be ashamed of. I've seen how it can make a difference in people's lives. One patient of mine, a nineteen-year-old girl, ⓑwas going through a difficult time after her mom passed away. Cases like this make me so ⓒproudly to be part of the program. It is truly a rewarding experience ⓓto help people make positive changes in their lives. It's inspiring to see the influence ⓔwhat the Friendship Bench program has had.
solution: ⓒ 「make+목적어+목적격보어」에서 보어 자리에는 형용사가 와야 하므로 proudly를 proud로 고친다(make me proud). ⓔ 선행사 the influence를 받는 목적격 관계대명사가 필요하므로 what을 that(또는 which)으로 고친다. ⓐ 동명사 주어, ⓑ 과거진행, ⓓ 「It is ~ to부정사」·「help+목적어+동사원형」은 모두 적법하다.

body:
다음 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?

Something had to be done to deal with the loss of Melbourne's trees. In 2012, the city government announced its Urban Forest Strategy plan. It set the ambitious goal of planting more than 3,000 trees every year for the next twenty years. The plan also involved the creation of an online map called the Urban Forest Visual. This interactive map shows the location of every single tree in the city's parks and along its roads. It uses colors and symbols to indicate each tree's age and genus.
solution:
본문에서 이 계획은 앞으로 20년 동안 '매년(every year)' 3,000그루 '이상(more than)'을 심는 것을 목표로 했다. 따라서 over 3,000 trees a year for two decades로 바꿔 쓴 ②가 일치한다.
① '20년 동안 총 3,000그루'가 아니라 '매년 3,000그루 이상'이다.
③ 지도는 공원뿐 아니라 도로변(along its roads)의 나무 위치도 보여 준다.
④ 색과 기호로 나타내는 것은 나무의 나이(age)와 속(genus)이고, 건강 상태는 나타내지 않는다.
⑤ 지도는 가장 오래된 나무만이 아니라 모든 나무(every single tree)의 위치를 보여 준다.
choices: The plan aimed to plant a total of 3,000 trees over twenty years.
The plan set a goal of planting over 3,000 trees a year for two decades.
The Urban Forest Visual shows only the trees in the city's parks.
The Urban Forest Visual uses colors to show each tree's health condition.
The Urban Forest Visual shows the location of only the oldest trees.

body:
다음 글을 읽고 답할 수 없는 질문은?

The story behind these emails begins with Melbourne's Urban Forest Strategy plan, a response to Australia's millennium drought. This drought lasted from the late 1990s to 2010. By the time it ended, 40 percent of the city's 77,000 trees were in a state of declining health. The loss of canopy cover is a major threat to urban environments because it raises temperatures. Higher temperatures in cities can be dangerous for residents, as they increase the risk of heat exhaustion.
solution:
① 가뭄은 1990년대 후반부터 2010년까지 이어졌으므로 2010년에 끝났다.
② 가뭄이 끝났을 때 멜버른의 나무 77,000그루 중 40퍼센트가 건강이 나빠지는 상태였다.
③ 수관(canopy) 손실은 기온을 높이기 때문에 도시 환경에 큰 위협이 된다.
⑤ 도시의 높은 기온은 주민들의 열탈진(heat exhaustion) 위험을 높인다.
④ 잃은 나무를 대신하려고 몇 그루를 심었는지는 이 글에 나오지 않는다(식재 목표는 이 글 뒤에 이어지는 부분에 나온다). 따라서 답할 수 없는 질문은 ④이다.
choices: When did Australia's millennium drought end?
What percentage of Melbourne's trees were in declining health after the drought?
Why is the loss of canopy cover a major threat to urban environments?
How many trees did Melbourne plant to replace the ones it had lost?
What risk can higher temperatures in cities increase for residents?

body:
다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?

Dear Tree,
Whenever I walk past you, your beautiful leaves bring a smile to my face. Whenever I stop in front of you and take a deep breath of fresh air, I appreciate the oxygen that you produce. By the way, I noticed that a family of birds has made a nest in your branches. It's so kind of you to provide them with a home. I hope that more people realize how important you and all the other trees are to the environment. Have a nice day!
Believe it or not, trees in Melbourne, Australia receive emails like this all the time.
solution:
글쓴이는 새 가족이 이미 나뭇가지에 둥지를 지은 것(has made a nest)을 보았고, 나무가 새들에게 보금자리를 마련해 준 것을 칭찬했다. 새들이 아직 둥지 틀 곳을 찾고 있다는 ③은 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는다.
① 나무 옆을 지나갈 때마다 아름다운 잎이 글쓴이를 미소 짓게 한다.
② 글쓴이는 나무가 만드는 산소에 고마워한다(appreciate the oxygen).
④ 글쓴이는 더 많은 사람이 나무가 환경에 얼마나 중요한지 깨닫기를 바란다.
⑤ 멜버른의 나무들은 이런 이메일을 늘(all the time) 받는다.
choices: The tree's leaves make the writer smile when the writer walks past it.
The writer is thankful for the oxygen produced by the tree.
The writer noticed some birds still looking for a place to nest in the tree.
The writer wishes more people knew how important trees are to nature.
Trees in Melbourne often receive emails similar to this one.

body:
다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?

Locally, the tree mail phenomenon, which started from the Urban Forest Strategy, has inspired many Melbourne residents to offer their own ideas about building an environmentally friendly urban environment. Some have even volunteered to measure trees and monitor animals for nature programs in the city. Meanwhile, the Urban Forest Strategy's tree planting project has remained on track, and canopy cover is predicted to increase from 23 percent in 2012 to 40 percent by the year 2040. As a result, residents will be happier and healthier as they move toward a greener future.
solution:
본문에서 tree mail 현상은 Urban Forest Strategy에서 시작되었다(which started from the Urban Forest Strategy). 즉 전략이 먼저 있었고 tree mail이 뒤에 생겼으므로, tree mail 때문에 시가 전략을 시작했다는 ③은 인과 관계를 뒤집은 것이라 일치하지 않는다.
① tree mail 현상에 자극받아 많은 주민이 친환경 도시 환경을 만드는 아이디어를 내놓았다.
② 일부 주민은 자연 프로그램을 위해 나무를 측정하고 동물을 관찰하는 일에 자원했다.
④ 나무 심기 프로젝트는 순조롭게 진행되고 있다(has remained on track).
⑤ 수관 피복률은 2012년 23퍼센트에서 2040년 40퍼센트로 늘어날 것으로 예측되므로 17퍼센트포인트 증가한다.
choices: Many residents suggested ideas for an eco-friendly city due to tree mail.
Some residents offered to help measure trees and observe animals.
The tree mail phenomenon led the city to start the Urban Forest Strategy.
The tree planting project has been going as planned so far.
Canopy cover is expected to grow by 17 percentage points from 2012 to 2040.

다음 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?

In the 19th century, the Industrial Revolution caused a sharp rise in factory production in the United States. As the demand for workers grew, many new positions were filled by children. By 1900, about twenty percent of all children in the United States were employed, and some of those working in factories were only four years old. Factory owners preferred child workers for several reasons. For example, children could be paid less than adult workers, and they were also less likely to go on strike.
solution: 산업혁명으로 공장 생산이 '급증'했고 1900년에 전체 아동의 '약 20%'가 고용되었으며, 일부는 겨우 네 살이었다. 공장주가 아이를 선호한 이유로 임금이 적고 '파업할 가능성이 낮다'는 점이 제시된다. 따라서 ⑤가 일치한다. ①②③④는 본문과 반대이거나 사실과 어긋난다.
choices: The Industrial Revolution caused factory production in the U.S. to drop sharply.
By 1900, all children in the United States were employed in factories.
Every child working in a factory was at least ten years old.
Factory owners paid children more than they paid adult workers.
One reason owners hired children was that they were less likely to go on strike.

다음 대화의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?

Noah: These days, more and more teenagers get their news from social media instead of newspapers or TV.
Mia: I like that change. Social media makes it faster and easier to find and share news.
Ryan: I agree it's convenient, but people often share stories without checking whether they're true, so false information can spread quickly.
Emma: Exactly. That's why I still trust traditional news sources more. We shouldn't pass along news online before making sure it is accurate.
solution: Ryan은 소셜미디어가 '편리하다(convenient)'는 점에는 동의하면서 '거짓 정보가 빠르게 퍼진다'는 부정적 면을 지적한다. 속도가 느리다고 말한 적은 없으므로 ③이 일치하지 않는다. 나머지 선지는 각 화자의 말과 일치한다.
choices: Noah says teenagers increasingly get news from social media rather than newspapers or TV.
Mia thinks social media has made finding and sharing news faster and easier.
Ryan argues that social media is too slow for sharing news quickly.
Ryan is worried that false information can spread quickly on social media.
Emma trusts traditional news sources and warns against sharing unverified news online.

다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?

In the 1880s, industry began to grow rapidly along the Cuyahoga River in the city of Cleveland. This industrial growth provided steady jobs to people in the area. Meanwhile, steel mills and factories started dumping large amounts of waste into the river. Although the river became polluted, most people simply regarded this as a sign of the area's economic success. In June 1969, the polluted river caught fire, but few people in Cleveland cared. This was because fires had been recorded on the Cuyahoga more than ten times before, and some of them had been much worse.
solution: 본문에서 대부분의 사람들은 오염된 강을 '그 지역 경제 성공의 신호'로 여겼고 1969년 화재에도 관심이 거의 없었다. 따라서 '심각한 경고로 보고 즉각적 변화를 요구했다'는 ④는 일치하지 않는다. 나머지는 모두 본문과 일치한다.
choices: Industry grew rapidly along the Cuyahoga River in the 1880s.
The industrial growth provided steady jobs to people in the area.
Steel mills and factories dumped large amounts of waste into the river.
Most people saw the polluted river as a serious warning and demanded immediate change.
The 1969 fire drew little attention because earlier fires had been worse.

Lewis Hine, a teacher and photographer, wanted to reveal how cruel the child labor system was. So he quit his teaching job and started to work for the National Child Labor Committee as an investigative photographer. He gained access to factories by pretending to have different jobs like insurance agent or fire inspector. Once inside, he would photograph the children working there. He would also ask their names and ages and record information about their living and working conditions. From 1908 to 1912, he secretly gathered information and took photographs to expose factory owners who were taking advantage of helpless children.
solution: 본문에 Hine이 원래 교사(①)였고, National Child Labor Committee에서 일했으며(②), 보험 설계사·화재 조사관 등으로 위장해 들어갔고(③), 1908년부터 1912년까지 활동한(④) 사실이 나온다. 그러나 그가 '총 몇 명의 아이를 촬영했는지'는 언급되지 않으므로 ⑤는 답할 수 없다.
choices: What job did Lewis Hine have before working for the National Child Labor Committee?
For what organization did Hine work as an investigative photographer?
How did Hine manage to get inside the factories?
During which years did Hine secretly gather information and take photographs?
How many children in total did Hine photograph during his investigation?

다음 글을 가장 바르게 이해한 사람은?

The 1969 Cuyahoga River fire soon became famous, thanks to an article published in Time magazine that year. The article featured a shocking photograph of flames and smoke rising from the river. However, this was not a photograph of the 1969 fire, which was put out so quickly that nobody took a picture of it. In fact, it was a picture of a much worse fire that had occurred on the river several years earlier. Still, the image had a great impact on people. More and more Americans became aware of the need to protect the environment, and the shocking image sparked public anger about water pollution. As a result, the fire became a symbol of pollution, and a national environmental event held on April 22, 1970 later became known as the first Earth Day.
solution: Time지의 충격적 사진은 1969년 화재가 아니라 '몇 년 전에 일어난 더 심각한 화재'를 찍은 것이다. 따라서 ③이 옳다. 1969년 화재는 빨리 진화되어 사진이 없고(①② 오답), 그 이미지가 큰 영향을 주었으며(④ 오답), 지구의 날 행사는 1969년 '이후'인 1970년에 열렸다(⑤ 오답).
choices: Jisu: The photograph in Time magazine was an actual picture of the 1969 fire.
Minho: The 1969 fire was photographed because it kept burning for a long time.
Yuna: The famous photograph actually showed an earlier, more serious fire on the river.
Sora: The image had almost no effect on how Americans viewed water pollution.
Dohun: The first Earth Day was held several years before the 1969 fire.

윗글의 제목으로 알맞은 것은?

We tried to practice once a week through a video chat app, but it wasn't easy. We all lived in different time zones, so finding a time that suited everyone was hard. The app also had audio problems that made us out of sync. Instead of giving up, we came up with a new idea. We decided to build our songs one part at a time, as if in a virtual music factory. First I played the melody on my keyboard and sent it to Singaporean Sam. He added his singing and passed it on to American Sam, who put in his guitar part. Finally, Samantha completed the song with her drums.
solution: 시차와 음질 문제로 함께 연습하기 어려웠지만 포기하지 않고 각자 자기 파트를 차례로 녹음해 노래를 완성하는 '가상 음악 공장' 방식을 고안했다는 글이다. 멀리 떨어진 멤버들이 음악을 만들어 낸 영리한 방법을 담고 있으므로 제목으로는 ②가 가장 알맞다. ③④⑤는 글의 세부 소재일 뿐이고 ①은 내용과 반대이다.
choices: ① Giving Up Our Dream of a Band
② A Clever Way to Make Music from Afar
③ The Best Time Zone for Online Practice
④ How to Fix Audio Problems in Video Apps
⑤ Learning to Play the Keyboard Online

윗글의 주제로 알맞은 것은?

When I searched "Sam Lee" on a social media website, I was amazed to find so many people with that name all over the world. Just for fun, I sent friend requests to several of them, and many accepted. As I looked through their profiles, I noticed that a number of these Sam Lees loved music. One was a Singaporean who enjoyed singing, another was a Canadian drummer, and another was an American guitarist. People who had nothing in common but a name turned out to share the same passion.
solution: 'Sam Lee'라는 같은 이름을 가진 세계 각지의 사람들이 음악이라는 공통의 관심사를 가지고 있었다는 내용이다. 따라서 주제로는 '같은 이름과 음악을 향한 사랑을 공유하는 낯선 이들'인 ③이 알맞다. 나머지는 글에 언급되지 않았거나 세부 정보에 불과하다.
choices: ① the difficulty of finding real friends online
② how a common last name became popular worldwide
③ strangers who share the same name and a love of music
④ the best way to search for musicians on social media
⑤ why so many people around the world are named Sam Lee

Having a large number of friends is not always the best thing. True friendships are built over time, usually with the people you see most often. Such friends know the real you and let you be yourself. Rather than always chasing after new friends, it is wiser to think about how to treasure the ones you already have. What matters in friendship is not how many friends you have, but how much they mean to you.
solution: 친구가 많다고 늘 좋은 것은 아니며, 새 친구를 쫓기보다 이미 있는 친구를 소중히 여겨야 한다고 말한다. 마지막 문장에서 중요한 것은 친구의 '수'가 아니라 그들이 주는 '의미'라고 못 박고 있으므로 요지는 ③이다. ⑤는 세부 내용일 뿐 글 전체의 주장이 아니다.

When it came to choosing songs, the members of our band took turns. Because each of us prefers a different genre and comes from a different culture, we all ended up learning a lot about various kinds of music. Building each song part by part was not always easy, but it was interesting and a lot of fun. Through this process, we grew closer and discovered music we had never known before.

Since the band members came from different cultures and (A)__________ different genres, taking turns to choose songs helped them (B)__________ many new kinds of music while growing closer.
solution: 각 멤버가 서로 다른 문화 출신이고 서로 다른 장르를 '좋아했기(enjoyed)' 때문에, 돌아가며 곡을 고르는 과정에서 새로운 음악을 많이 '발견하게(discover)' 되었다는 흐름이다. 따라서 (A)-(B)는 enjoyed–discover인 ②가 알맞다. 나머지는 글의 긍정적 결과와 맞지 않는다.

During World War II, there was a group of people who risked everything to protect priceless works of art from ruin. In 1943, around 345 people from 14 different Allied nations* came together to form the Monuments, Fine Arts, and Archives (MFAA) program. They were not trained soldiers but scholars and experts of various kinds, such as professors, historians, and architects. These brave men and women volunteered to protect Europe's cultural heritage and became known as the "Monuments Men."
*Allied nations (1, 2차 세계대전 때의) 연합국
solution: 이 글은 교수, 역사가, 건축가 등 여러 분야의 전문가들이 MFAA 프로그램을 만들고, 유럽의 문화유산을 지키는 일에 자원해 '모뉴먼츠 맨'으로 알려지게 되었다는 내용이다. 이들은 훈련받은 군인이 아니었다고 했으므로 ②는 글과 맞지 않는다. ⑤처럼 군사 동맹을 맺었다는 내용도 글에 없다. 따라서 요지는 ③이다.
choices: 전쟁 중에는 예술 작품 보호보다 군사 작전이 우선되어야 한다.
연합국 군인들은 예술 작품을 보호하기 위해 특수 훈련을 받았다.
다양한 분야의 전문가들이 유럽의 문화유산을 지키기 위해 자원하여 모뉴먼츠 맨이 되었다.
제2차 세계대전 중 많은 학자들이 전쟁을 피해 유럽을 떠났다.
1943년에 14개 연합국이 모여 새로운 군사 동맹을 결성했다.

다음 글의 제목으로 가장 알맞은 것은?

Did you know that there are over 7,000 languages currently being used around the world? Most of these languages are spoken by very small groups of people, and half of them could disappear within the next generation. This would be a great loss because language plays a big role in connecting people's identity to their culture. This is why some organizations work to preserve them. For example, a nonprofit organization called Wikitongues has set the goal of preserving all languages that are in danger of being lost. The organization works to achieve this by recording videos of individuals speaking these languages and making mother-tongue resources more accessible.
solution: 이 글은 많은 언어가 다음 세대 안에 사라질 위기에 있으며, Wikitongues 같은 단체가 이런 언어를 보존하려고 노력한다는 내용이다. 따라서 제목으로는 '사라지기 전에 소멸 위기 언어 구하기'가 알맞다. ④는 7,000이라는 숫자만 따온 오답이고, ⑤는 영상 녹화라는 세부 내용만 따온 오답이다.
choices: Saving Endangered Languages Before They Disappear
Why Everyone Should Learn a Second Language
The History of the World's 7,000 Languages
Making Videos: A New Hobby for Language Learners

다음 글의 제목으로 가장 알맞은 것은?

One of the largest collections of stolen items was hidden in the salt mines of Altaussee, Austria. Upon discovering its location, some of the Monuments Men rushed to the mines. They hoped to recover everything before it was too late.
Meanwhile, the Nazi leader who was in charge of the area tried to destroy everything by setting off large explosives inside the mines. This could have been disastrous. Luckily, some local miners found the explosives in the mines and came up with a plan to protect their livelihood. They secretly removed the large explosives and put smaller ones at the entrances. Once they went off, the Nazi leader believed that everything was destroyed. However, while the small explosions sealed off the entrances, they left the rest of the mines and the works of art unharmed.
solution: 나치 지도자가 대형 폭발물로 광산을 파괴하려 했지만, 지역 광부들이 폭발물을 몰래 작은 것으로 바꿔 입구만 막히게 했다. 그 덕분에 광산 안의 예술 작품들은 무사할 수 있었다는 것이 글의 중심 내용이다. ④는 폭발물 계획을 세운 주체를 모뉴먼츠 맨으로 바꾼 함정이다. ⑤처럼 소금 광산이 최적의 보관 장소였던 이유는 글에 나오지 않는다.
choices: How the Nazis Built Secret Mines in Austria
The Miners' Clever Plan That Saved Hidden Treasures
A Failed Attempt to Find the Altaussee Salt Mines
The Monuments Men's Explosion Plan Against the Nazis
Why Salt Mines Were the Best Place to Store Art

다음 글의 요지로 가장 알맞은 것은?

The efforts of the Monuments Men did not end with the war. For several years, they continued the work of recovering cultural treasures and identifying where they had been stolen from. In the end, the Monuments Men returned more than five million works of art and objects of cultural importance to their places of origin.
Not everything that was stolen by the Nazis has been found, but what the Monuments Men accomplished is truly amazing. Without this determined group, the search for stolen works of art might never have begun. In addition, countless historical and cultural landmarks would have been lost forever due to the destruction of war. It is worth remembering the Monuments Men's contribution to the preservation of cultural heritage. Thanks to their efforts, many incredible cultural sites and works of art have survived and can still be appreciated to this day.
solution: 필자는 모뉴먼츠 맨이 전쟁 후에도 수백만 점의 문화재를 되찾아 돌려보냈다고 말한다. 그리고 'It is worth remembering ~' 문장으로 이들의 공헌을 기억할 가치가 있다고 강조한다. ①은 'Not everything ... has been found'와 맞지 않는다. ⑤는 가정법 문장의 내용을 지나치게 일반화한 오답이다.
choices: 나치가 약탈한 예술 작품은 결국 모두 원래 장소로 돌아갔다.
문화유산 보존에 기여한 모뉴먼츠 맨의 업적은 기억할 가치가 있다.
전쟁이 끝난 뒤에는 문화재 복원보다 도시 재건이 우선이다.
예술 작품을 제대로 감상하려면 작품의 출처를 알아야 한다.
전쟁으로 사라진 랜드마크는 다시는 복원될 수 없다.

body:
다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약할 때, 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 알맞게 짝지어진 것은?

The Monuments Men thought that it would take about one year to transport everything they found to a safe location. However, because control of the area was going to change at the end of the war, they would have access to the mines for just two months. With insufficient packing supplies and only a few trucks, the transporting mission seemed impossible. Not only that, but food was in short supply. Even without eating proper meals, they worked up to twenty hours a day. They used coats and gas masks as packing materials and did everything they could to accomplish this vital mission in time.
In the end, the Monuments Men succeeded in rescuing thousands of stolen works of art, including important pieces such as Jan van Eyck's Adoration of the Mystic Lamb, Johannes Vermeer's The Astronomer, and Michelangelo's Madonna of Bruges.

→ Although the Monuments Men faced (A)__________ circumstances such as limited time and a lack of supplies and food, their (B)__________ efforts led to the successful rescue of thousands of stolen artworks.

   (A)            (B)
solution: 모뉴먼츠 맨에게는 두 달이라는 짧은 시간만 있었고, 포장재와 트럭, 식량도 모자랐다. 그러므로 (A)에는 '혹독한(harsh)' 상황이 알맞다. 그런데도 그들은 하루 최대 20시간씩 일하며 최선을 다했으므로, (B)에는 '헌신적인(devoted)'이 알맞다. ②와 ⑤는 (A)는 맞지만 (B)가 글의 내용과 반대이고, ①은 (B)는 맞지만 (A)가 틀린 함정이다.

다음 글의 요지로 가장 알맞은 것은?

Although the new residents would have to pay for the renovations, the government’s plan soon attracted many applicants. Apparently, it was not just the idea of one-euro apartments that people found attractive. They were also excited by the opportunity to use their creativity to improve the building.
In the end, 42 new families moved into Wallisblok. The government’s bold plan was a success. The residents transformed the old, worn-out building into 42 unique apartments with a community garden and rooftop terrace. The surrounding area soon began to improve as well. Today, Wallisblok is one of the most desirable places to live in Rotterdam.
solution:

① 본문은 싼 가격'만'이 이유가 아니라고 말하므로 일부만 맞는 오답이다.

In the early 20th century, there was an area in the northern part of Amsterdam that was full of shipyards and factories. Over time, the shipyards closed down, and the work once done at the factories was moved abroad. As a result, the area was left abandoned and polluted for years.
Wanting to do something to improve the area, the city purchased an abandoned shipyard called De Ceuvel. However, city officials did not know what to do with it. So they turned to the public for help by asking for plans that would achieve two primary goals. First, the plan had to include a method to clean up the land and turn it into a sustainable development. Second, it had to suggest a way to transform the site into a creative workspace.
solution:
조선소와 공장이 사라진 뒤 지역이 버려지고 오염되자, 시는 이 지역을 개선하려고 De Ceuvel을 사들였다. 그러나 활용 방법을 몰라 시민들에게 (1) 땅을 정화해 지속 가능한 개발지로 만들고 (2) 창의적 작업 공간으로 바꾸는 계획을 요청했다. 따라서 주제는 ②이다.
① 첫 단락의 배경 설명만 키운 오답이다.
③ 시 공무원들은 활용 방법을 몰라 시민들에게 도움을 청했다(turned to the public for help). 직접 정화했다는 말은 본문과 맞지 않는다.
④ 계획이 갖춰야 할 조건만 제시되었을 뿐, 실제 설계와 변화는 이 글에 나오지 않는다.
⑤ 지속 가능한 개발은 계획의 조건 중 하나로만 언급되고, 산업 구조에 미친 영향은 다루지 않는다.
choices: 조선소와 공장이 사라지면서 암스테르담 북부 지역이 쇠퇴한 원인
버려진 지역을 살리려고 시가 두 가지 목표를 내걸고 계획을 공모한 과정

다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 알맞은 것은?

For years, the neighborhood was known for its high crime rates. Many apartments in Wallisblok were abandoned and then taken over by people who lived in them illegally. At first, the local government thought that the best solution was simply to tear the building down and build a new one in its place. However, having a limited budget, the government was unable to do so and had to come up with a new plan. The plan was to sell the empty apartments for one euro each. The only condition was that people who bought these apartments needed to renovate them.
Although the new residents would have to pay for these renovations, the government’s plan soon attracted many applicants. Apparently, it was not just the idea of one-euro apartments that people found attractive. They were also excited by the opportunity to use their creativity to improve the building.
In the end, 42 new families moved into Wallisblok. The government’s bold plan was a success. The residents transformed the old, worn-out building into 42 unique apartments with a community garden and rooftop terrace. The surrounding area soon began to improve as well. Today, Wallisblok is one of the most desirable places to live in Rotterdam.

→ Unable to afford a new building, the government sold empty apartments for one euro on the condition that buyers would (A)_______ them, and the residents’ creativity turned Wallisblok into a(n) (B)_______ place to live.

   (A)            (B)
solution:
(A) 정부는 예산이 부족해 건물을 새로 지을 수 없었다. 그래서 빈 아파트를 1유로에 팔면서 구매자가 직접 수리해야 한다는(needed to renovate them) 조건을 붙였다. renovate를 바꿔 쓴 repair(수리하다)가 알맞다. demolish(철거하다)는 정부가 처음에 생각했다가 예산 때문에 포기한 방안이다. rent(임대하다)와 abandon(버리다)은 본문의 조건과 맞지 않는다.
(B) 주민들의 창의성 덕분에 Wallisblok은 로테르담에서 가장 살고 싶은 곳 중 하나(one of the most desirable places to live)가 되었다. 따라서 popular(인기 있는)가 알맞다. dangerous(위험한)는 범죄율이 높던 과거의 모습이고, crowded(붐비는)와 isolated(고립된)는 본문에 근거가 없다.
따라서 정답은 ③이다.

The story behind these emails begins with Melbourne's Urban Forest Strategy plan, a response to Australia's millennium drought. This drought lasted from the late 1990s to 2010. By the time it ended, 40 percent of the city's 77,000 trees were in a state of declining health. Furthermore, the overall number of trees was decreasing.
As a result, the amount of shade provided by trees within the city, also known as canopy cover, decreased. The loss of canopy cover is a major threat to urban environments because it raises temperatures. Higher temperatures in cities can be dangerous for residents, as they increase the risk of heat exhaustion*. They also lead to a rise in the use of air conditioning. This speeds up climate change by increasing energy consumption and greenhouse gas emissions.
*heat exhaustion 열탈진

Something had to be done to deal with the loss of Melbourne’s trees. In 2012, the city government announced its Urban Forest Strategy plan. This interactive map shows the location of every single tree in the city’s parks and along its roads. It uses colors and symbols to indicate each tree’s age and genus. Also, users can click on a tree to find out its species and even send it an email. At first, the “Email this tree” function had a specific purpose. It was designed to allow people to easily inform council workers about trees that were damaged or in poor health.

solution: Grandma Moyo는 자신이 상담한 19세 소녀가 회복한 사례를 들고, 마지막 문장에서 사람들이 긍정적인 변화를 만들도록 돕는 것이 정말 보람 있는 경험이라고 말한다. 따라서 요지는 ④이다. ①은 '부끄러워할 일이 아니다'라는 본문 내용과 반대이고, ③은 사례의 세부 내용을 지나치게 일반화한 선지다.
choices: ① 정신 건강 문제로 도움을 구하는 것은 부끄러운 일이므로 신중해야 한다.
② 가족을 잃은 슬픔은 시간이 지나면 저절로 치유된다.
③ 젊은이들은 창업을 통해 어려움을 극복해야 한다.
④ 사람들이 삶에서 긍정적인 변화를 이루도록 돕는 것은 보람 있는 일이다.
⑤ 상담은 전문 의사만이 효과적으로 할 수 있다.

body:
다음 글의 내용을 아래와 같이 요약할 때, 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 알맞은 것은?

Host: Oh, so that was the beginning of it. Could you explain to us how the Friendship Bench program works?
Dr. Chibanda: Certainly. The program was created as a way to provide accessible mental health services. It offers talk therapy sessions to people dealing with issues such as depression or anxiety. The sessions are free and are provided by respected elderly women from the community. These women, called “grandmothers,” volunteer to sit with patients at the benches, listen to their stories, and provide them with emotional support.
Host: What a wonderful idea! How did these amazing grandmothers become a part of your program?
Dr. Chibanda: Grandmothers were chosen for our program because they are deeply connected to the community. Moreover, they have all the qualities of a counselor, such as excellent listening skills, empathy, and the ability to engage in meaningful discussions. They are also very reliable, which is important for our efforts to support mental health.

[요약]
The Friendship Bench program provides free talk therapy, and grandmothers were selected for it because they have strong (A)__________ with the community and the (B)__________ needed to be good counselors.

    (A)          (B)
solution: 할머니들은 지역 사회와 깊이 연결되어 있고(deeply connected to the community), 경청 능력과 공감 능력 같은 상담자의 자질(all the qualities of a counselor)을 모두 갖추어서 선발되었다. 따라서 (A)에는 connections, (B)에는 qualities가 들어간다. ③의 skills는 (B)에 들어갈 수 있지만 (A)의 differences가 본문과 맞지 않는다.

body:
다음 글의 주제로 가장 알맞은 것은?

Host: On today’s show, we are going to learn about special park benches in Zimbabwe called Friendship Benches. We have two special guests. First, please welcome the founder of the Friendship Bench program, Dr. Dixon Chibanda. Can you tell us what inspired you to come up with the program?
Dr. Chibanda: Sure. The idea came from an experience I had as a psychiatrist. One of my patients had become severely depressed. However, she couldn’t get help because she was unable to afford the bus ride to the hospital. This shocked me, as I had never considered such a problem before. In fact, it is difficult for many people in Zimbabwe to pay for transportation and receive medical treatment. Furthermore, there has been a lack of psychiatrists in the country for many years. When the Friendship Bench program started in 2006, there were only eleven psychiatrists serving Zimbabwe’s population of over twelve million people. I needed to find a way to bring psychiatry into the community.
solution: Dr. Chibanda는 교통비를 낼 수 없어 치료를 받지 못한 환자를 겪으면서 짐바브웨의 교통비 부담과 정신과 의사 부족 문제를 깨달았다. 그래서 정신 의학을 지역 사회로 가져갈 방법이 필요했다고 말한다. 따라서 주제는 ①이다. ②는 버스비라는 세부 소재만 따로 떼어 낸 선지이고, ③~⑤는 본문에 근거가 없다.
choices: ① the problems that led Dr. Chibanda to bring psychiatry into the community
② the reasons why bus fares in Zimbabwe have increased
③ the history of psychiatric hospitals in Zimbabwe
④ the daily life of a psychiatrist working at a city hospital
⑤ the ways patients can overcome depression on their own

body:
다음 글의 제목으로 가장 알맞은 것은?

Host: That’s interesting! What happens after patients complete their sessions with the grandmothers?
Dr. Chibanda: When the sessions with the grandmothers are over, patients are encouraged to join a community support group made up of former patients of the program. The members of these groups can easily relate to and support one another. This is because most of them come from the same community and have experienced similar struggles.
Host: That sounds like a great way to continue the support and build a sense of community. And the program has been incredibly successful, right?
Dr. Chibanda: That’s correct. In 2022, we provided face-to-face counseling to about 90,000 patients in Zimbabwe. Now, Friendship Benches are available in more than twenty different regions around the country. Our vision is for everyone to have a Friendship Bench within walking distance, and we are working hard to make it happen. We’ve also started expanding the program, and we now offer online counseling through an app. This has helped us reach even more people.
solution: 글의 앞부분은 상담이 끝난 뒤 지원 모임을 통해 도움이 이어진다는 내용이고, 뒷부분은 국내 20여 개 지역으로의 확대와 온라인 상담 같은 프로그램의 성장을 다룬다. 이 두 내용을 모두 담은 ④가 제목으로 알맞다. ①은 확대 범위가 '나라 안(around the country)'인데 '전 세계'로 바꾼 함정이다. ③은 앱이 대면 상담을 '대체했다'고 왜곡했는데, 본문에서 앱은 대면 상담에 더해진 것이다. ②는 지원 모임 구성원(former patients)과 상담자(grandmothers)를 섞어 놓은 오답이다.
choices: ① From One Bench to the World: The Program’s Global Expansion
② How Former Patients Become Grandmother Counselors
③ An App That Has Replaced Face-to-Face Counseling
④ Ongoing Support and Growing Reach of the Friendship Bench
⑤ Why Zimbabwe Lacks Enough Mental Health Services

body:
다음 글의 내용을 아래와 같이 요약할 때, 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 알맞은 것은?

Host: That’s very kind of you. Can you tell us about your experience as a grandmother for the Friendship Bench program?
Grandma Moyo: It’s been wonderful. Seeking help for mental health problems is nothing to be ashamed of. I’ve seen how it can make a difference in people’s lives. One patient of mine, a nineteen-year-old girl, was going through a difficult time after her mom passed away. I counseled her and helped her begin her recovery journey. Now her life is back on track, and she has even started her own business! Cases like this make me so proud to be part of the program. It is such a rewarding experience to help people make positive changes in their lives.
Host: Thanks for sharing your experiences with us today, Grandma Moyo. It’s truly inspiring to see the influence that the Friendship Bench program has had. And it’s all thanks to the hard work of people like you and Dr. Chibanda.

[요약]
Grandma Moyo says people should not feel (A)__________ about seeking help for mental health problems, and she finds her work (B)__________ because she can see patients like a young girl recover and make positive changes in their lives.

    (A)          (B)
solution: 'Seeking help for mental health problems is nothing to be ashamed of.'에 따르면 사람들은 도움을 구하는 것을 부끄러워할(ashamed) 필요가 없다. 또 마지막 문장에서 사람들을 돕는 것이 보람 있는(rewarding) 경험이라고 했으므로 답은 ②이다. ①의 proud는 본문에 나오는 단어지만, 프로그램의 일원인 것에 대한 Moyo 자신의 감정이라서 (A)의 의미와 맞지 않는 함정이다. ③은 (A)는 맞지만 (B)가 본문 내용과 반대다.

body:
다음 글에 소개된 Friendship Bench 프로그램에 관한 설명으로 옳은 것은?

The Friendship Bench program helps people who have mental health difficulties, including depression and anxiety. People can talk about their problems with elderly women who are respected in their community. These volunteers are known as grandmothers. They listen carefully and offer emotional support while sitting with patients on benches. Patients do not have to pay for these conversations.
solution: 지문에서 할머니 봉사자들은 환자들의 이야기를 주의 깊게 듣고 정서적 지지를 제공한다고 설명한다. 따라서 ②가 정답이다. ①은 우울증뿐 아니라 불안 등도 지원 대상이므로 틀리다. ③은 상담을 제공하는 사람과 받는 사람의 역할이 뒤바뀌었다. ④는 상담이 무료라는 내용과 반대이며, ⑤는 상담 상대가 의사로 제한되지 않고 할머니 봉사자라는 점에서 틀리다.
choices: The program provides support only to people suffering from depression.
The grandmothers listen to patients and provide emotional support.
The grandmothers receive counseling from patients in their community.
Patients must pay a small fee to receive emotional support.
The program requires patients to discuss their problems with doctors.

body:
다음 글의 Judith Moyo에 관한 설명으로 적절하지 않은 것은?

Judith Moyo, also known as Grandma Moyo, volunteers for the Friendship Bench program. Seeing people around her suffer from mental health difficulties gave her a reason to join. She wanted to offer support that could help them recover emotionally. She feels proud when she sees patients making positive changes in their lives.
solution: Moyo가 프로그램에 참여한 계기는 주변 사람들이 정신 건강 문제로 어려움을 겪는 모습을 보았기 때문이다. 자신의 정신 건강 문제에서 회복한 후 프로그램에 참여했다는 내용은 제시되어 있지 않으므로 ④가 정답이다. ①은 별명, ②는 봉사 활동, ③은 참여 동기, ⑤는 활동에서 느끼는 보람에 관한 내용으로 모두 지문과 일치한다.
choices: She is also known by the name Grandma Moyo.
She participates in the Friendship Bench program voluntarily.
She became interested in the program after seeing others struggle.
She joined the program after recovering from her own mental health difficulties.
She feels proud when the people she helps make positive changes.

body:
다음 글의 지원 그룹(support groups)에 관한 설명으로 옳은 것은?

Support can continue even after patients finish talking with the grandmothers. The Friendship Bench program encourages them to enter support groups consisting of people who previously received help through the program. Many group members belong to the same community and have faced similar difficulties. These shared experiences make it easier for them to understand and help each other.
solution: 지원 그룹은 이전에 프로그램을 통해 도움을 받은 사람들로 구성되며, 비슷한 어려움을 겪은 경험을 바탕으로 서로 이해하고 돕는다. 따라서 ③이 정답이다. ①은 상담 이후에도 지원이 이어진다는 내용과 맞지 않는다. ②는 구성원을 할머니 상담자로 잘못 설명했고, ④는 이전에 도움을 받은 사람들로 구성된다는 설명과 반대이다. ⑤는 지원 그룹이 상담을 대체한다는 근거가 없으므로 틀리다.
choices: The groups are formed before patients begin their counseling sessions.
The groups mainly consist of grandmothers who provide counseling.
The groups allow former patients to support one another.
The groups bring together people who have never received support.
The groups replace the counseling sessions offered by grandmothers.

body:
다음 글의 내용만으로는 답할 수 없는 질문은?

The Friendship Bench program uses grandmothers as volunteer counselors. Their strong ties to local people help explain this choice. They are good listeners, understand other people's feelings, and can have meaningful conversations. People can also depend on them. The program began with a small group of grandmothers, and the number of women trained to offer this support has since grown greatly.
solution: ①은 할머니들이 자원봉사 상담자로 활동한다는 내용에서 답할 수 있다. ②는 지역 주민과의 강한 유대 관계, 경청 능력, 공감 능력 등에서 답을 찾을 수 있다. ④는 경청 능력과 타인의 감정을 이해하는 능력 등으로 답할 수 있다. ⑤는 훈련받은 여성의 수가 크게 증가했다는 내용에서 확인할 수 있다. 반면 ③은 할머니들이 지역 주민의 신뢰를 얻은 구체적인 과정이나 방법을 묻는다. 지문에는 사람들이 할머니들에게 의지할 수 있다는 사실만 제시되어 있고, 신뢰를 형성한 과정은 설명되어 있지 않다. 따라서 정답은 ③이다.
choices: What role do the grandmothers play in the program?
What makes the grandmothers suitable for their role?
How have the grandmothers gained the trust of local people?
What personal qualities help the grandmothers support others?
How has the number of trained grandmothers changed over time?

body:
다음 글을 바탕으로 Dr. Chibanda가 지역 사회 중심의 정신 건강 지원 방식을 모색한 이유로 가장 적절한 것은?

An experience with a patient changed Dr. Chibanda's thinking. The patient needed help for severe depression but did not have enough money for transportation to the hospital. He realized that travel costs could keep people from receiving treatment. Zimbabwe also had too few psychiatrists to meet people's needs. These difficulties led him to look for a way to make mental health support available within communities.
solution: 첫째, 우울증이 심한 환자가 병원까지 갈 교통비가 없어 치료를 받기 어려웠다. 둘째, 짐바브웨에는 환자들의 수요를 충족할 만큼 정신과 전문의가 충분하지 않았다. Chibanda는 이러한 두 문제가 정신 건강 서비스에 대한 접근을 어렵게 한다고 판단하고 지역 사회 안에서 도움을 제공하는 방식을 모색했다. 따라서 두 가지 장애 요인을 종합한 ③이 정답이다. ①은 병원 수를 늘리려 했다는 근거가 없으며, ②는 전문의와의 만남을 늘리는 것이 직접적인 목적이라는 근거가 없다. ④는 전문의 양성에 초점을 맞춘다는 설명이 없고, ⑤는 두 문제의 심각성을 비교한 내용이 없으므로 적절하지 않다.
choices: He wanted to reduce travel costs by increasing the number of hospitals.
He believed that patients needed more opportunities to meet specialists.
He recognized that transportation costs and limited medical resources restricted access to care.
He concluded that local communities should focus mainly on training psychiatrists.
He thought that transportation problems were more serious than the shortage of specialists.

body:
다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?

A boy notices that his shirt has become tight and thinks frequent snacking, particularly late at night, may be the reason. He and a girl search for advice online. They learn that thirst can sometimes be mistaken for hunger. The advice also explains that missing daytime meals can increase hunger at night. If a snack is needed, fruit or nuts are suggested. The boy says he will try the advice.
solution: 지문은 낮 동안 식사를 거르면 밤에 배고픔이 더 심해질 수 있다고 설명한다. 따라서 낮 식사를 거르는 것을 간식 섭취를 줄이는 방법으로 권장한다는 ④는 지문의 내용과 일치하지 않는다. ①은 셔츠가 꽉 끼게 된 원인을 간식 습관에서 찾는 소년의 생각과 일치한다. ②는 소년과 소녀가 온라인에서 조언을 검색했다는 내용에 해당한다. ③은 갈증을 배고픔으로 착각할 수 있다는 설명과 일치한다. ⑤는 소년이 조언을 실천하겠다고 말한 내용과 일치한다.
choices: The boy suspects that his snacking habits have affected his body.
The boy and the girl look online for information about eating habits.
The advice explains that people may mistake thirst for hunger.
The advice recommends skipping meals during the day to reduce snacking.
The boy expresses his intention to follow the advice he has found.

body:
다음 글을 바탕으로 Friendship Bench 프로그램의 발전 방향을 추론한 내용으로 가장 적절한 것은?

The Friendship Bench program provides counseling in person and has also introduced counseling through an app. The online service has enabled the program to reach additional people. Patients who finish their sessions with grandmothers are encouraged to join groups of former patients, where shared experiences help members support one another. Friendship Benches have spread to many regions of Zimbabwe. However, the program is still working toward its vision of having a bench close enough for everyone to walk to.
solution: 이 문항은 지문의 여러 정보를 통합하여 프로그램의 발전 방향을 추론해야 한다. 첫째, 기존 대면 상담에 앱 상담을 추가하여 도움을 받을 수 있는 경로를 확대했다. 둘째, 상담을 마친 환자들에게 이전 환자들의 지원 그룹 참여를 권장하여 상담 이후에도 상호 지지가 이루어지도록 했다. 셋째, 벤치가 짐바브웨의 여러 지역으로 확산되었지만 모든 사람이 걸어서 이용할 수 있는 접근성은 아직 목표로 남아 있다. 따라서 다양한 지원 방식을 결합하면서 지역 사회의 접근성을 지속적으로 높이려 한다는 ④가 가장 적절하다. ①은 대면 상담의 유용성이 감소했다는 근거가 없고, ②는 지원 그룹이 지역 벤치의 필요성을 줄인다는 근거가 없다. ③은 기존 환자 지원을 신규 환자 접근보다 우선시한다는 근거가 없으며, ⑤는 자원봉사 상담을 지원 그룹으로 대체한다는 설명이 없으므로 틀리다.
choices: The program is shifting its attention from local counseling to online services because physical benches have become less useful.
The program is expanding access through digital services while using support groups to reduce the need for local benches.
The program is focusing on former patients because encouraging peer support has become more important than reaching new patients.
The program is combining different forms of support while continuing to improve access to services within local communities.
The program is expanding its services mainly by replacing volunteer counseling with independent support groups.

body:
다음 글에 제시된 두 사례를 비교한 내용으로 가장 적절한 것은?

A patient of Dr. Chibanda's suffered from severe depression but could not afford transportation to the hospital. This experience helped him recognize the need to bring mental health services closer to local people.

Grandma Moyo describes a patient who struggled after losing her mother. Through counseling, Moyo helped her take steps toward recovery. The young woman later got her life back on track and started a business. Moyo finds it rewarding to help people make positive changes and believes there is no shame in asking for mental health support.
solution: 첫 번째 사례의 핵심은 심한 우울증을 겪는 환자가 교통비 부족으로 병원에 가기 어려웠다는 점이다. 이를 통해 Chibanda는 치료 접근성을 높일 필요성을 깨달았다. 두 번째 사례의 핵심은 어머니를 잃은 후 어려움을 겪던 여성이 상담의 도움을 받아 회복을 향해 나아갔으며, 이후 삶을 다시 정비하고 사업을 시작했다는 점이다. 따라서 첫 사례는 치료 접근의 장애 요인을, 두 번째 사례는 상담 이후의 긍정적 변화를 보여 준다는 ①이 정답이다. ②에서 첫 환자가 치료를 원하지 않았다는 설명은 사실과 다르고, 둘째 환자가 경제적 지원을 받았다는 내용도 없다. ③은 지역 병원에 대한 선호와 사업 활동의 치료 효과를 지문에서 확인할 수 없다. ④는 첫 사례에 가족 문제가 제시되지 않았고, 두 사례로 우울증의 주요 원인을 일반화할 수 없다. ⑤는 두 사례의 어려움을 모두 경제적 문제로 환원하고 있어 타당하지 않다.
choices: The first case reveals a barrier to accessing treatment, while the second illustrates a positive outcome after counseling.
The first case emphasizes a patient's unwillingness to receive treatment, while the second highlights the importance of financial assistance.
The first case explains why patients prefer local hospitals, while the second shows why business activities improve mental health.
Both cases show that family problems are the main cause of depression and that community counseling provides a solution.
Both cases demonstrate that emotional recovery depends primarily on patients' ability to overcome financial difficulties.

body:
다음 우리말과 일치하도록 <보기>의 단어를 모두 활용하고 <조건>을 지켜 두 문장을 영작하시오.

나는 그 과제를 즐겼고, 내 반 친구들도 그랬다. 우리 자신에 관해 무엇을 발견할 수 있을지 생각해 보는 것은 흥미진진했다.

<보기> enjoy, classmate, exciting, think, discover, could, we

<조건>
• 첫 문장은 'so + 대동사 + 주어' 어순을 사용하여 9단어로 쓸 것
• 둘째 문장은 가주어 It과 진주어 to부정사를 사용하고, what이 이끄는 간접의문문을 포함하여 12단어로 쓸 것
• <보기>의 단어는 필요하면 형태를 바꿀 것 (한 단어를 두 번 이상 쓸 수 있음)
• 쉼표는 단어 수에 포함하지 않음
answer: I enjoyed the assignment, and so did my classmates. / It was exciting to think about what we could discover about ourselves.
solution:
[첫 문장] '나는 그 과제를 즐겼다'는 과거이므로 enjoy를 enjoyed로 쓴다. '~도 그랬다'는 'so + 대동사 + 주어'로 나타낸다. 앞 절의 동사가 일반동사의 과거형(enjoyed)이므로 대동사는 did를 쓴다(was, does는 틀림). 주어는 복수이므로 classmate를 classmates로 바꾸고 my를 붙인다. 도치 구문이므로 'so my classmates did'가 아니라 'so did my classmates'의 어순이 되어야 한다. → I enjoyed the assignment, and so did my classmates. (9단어)
[둘째 문장] '~하는 것은 흥미진진했다'는 가주어 It을 써서 It was exciting으로 시작하고, 진주어 to think about ~을 뒤에 둔다. '무엇을 발견할 수 있을지'는 전치사 about의 목적어 역할을 하는 간접의문문이므로 '의문사 + 주어 + 동사' 어순에 따라 what we could discover로 쓴다('what could we discover'는 틀림). '우리 자신에 관해'는 주어 we와 가리키는 대상이 같으므로 재귀대명사 ourselves를 써서 about ourselves로 쓴다. → It was exciting to think about what we could discover about ourselves. (12단어)

body:
다음 문장에서 밑줄 친 steady와 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?

The rapid industrial growth provided steady jobs to people living near the Cuyahoga River.
solution: steady는 문맥상 ‘꾸준한, 안정적인’이라는 뜻이다. 따라서 ‘정기적인, 지속적인’을 의미하는 regular가 가장 가깝다.

body:
빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 알맞은 것은?

The photograph ______ in Time magazine drew nationwide attention to the polluted river.
solution: 이 문장의 동사는 drew이므로 빈칸에는 또 다른 동사가 올 수 없다. 따라서 ①, ②, ⑤는 쓸 수 없다. 빈칸은 photograph를 뒤에서 수식한다. 사진은 잡지에 '실린' 대상이므로 수동의 뜻을 지닌 과거분사 featured가 알맞다. 현재분사 featuring은 능동(~을 싣는)의 뜻이므로 쓸 수 없다.

body:
빈칸에 들어갈 전치사로 가장 알맞은 것은?

Many people regarded the polluted river ______ a sign of economic success.
solution: 'A를 B로 여기다'는 「regard A as B」로 표현한다. 따라서 빈칸에는 as가 들어가야 한다.

body:
빈칸에 들어갈 관계사로 가장 알맞은 것은?

A national environmental event was held on April 22, 1970, ______ later became known as the first Earth Day.
solution: 빈칸 뒤 later became known에는 주어가 없다. 따라서 빈칸에는 주격 관계대명사가 필요하다. 완전한 절을 이끄는 관계부사 where와 when은 쓸 수 없다. 선행사를 포함하는 what은 앞에 선행사가 있으므로 쓸 수 없다. 쉼표 뒤 계속적 용법에는 that을 쓸 수 없으므로, 앞의 행사(event)를 부연 설명하는 which가 알맞다.

body: 다음 중 어법상 틀린 문장은?
solution: 사진은 스스로 찍는 것이 아니라 '찍히는' 대상이므로 수동태가 필요하다. 따라서 ⑤의 had taken은 had been taken으로 고쳐야 한다. ③은 「consider A B(A를 B로 여기다)」, ④는 「too ~ for 의미상 주어 to부정사」 구문으로 어법상 옳다.
choices: Industry began to grow rapidly along the river in the 1880s.
Factories dumped large amounts of waste into the river.
Many residents considered the pollution a sign of prosperity.
The 1969 fire was put out too quickly for anyone to photograph it.
The photograph in Time had taken during an earlier fire.

body:
다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

Industrial development ①created jobs, but factories also ②released waste into the river. Many residents ③interpreted the pollution as proof of prosperity. Because river fires had occurred repeatedly, the 1969 blaze seemed ④unprecedented to local people, and it initially received ⑤little concern.
solution: Because절에서 강의 화재가 이전에도 반복해서 일어났다고 했다. 그러니 주민들에게 1969년 화재는 익숙한 일이었을 것이고, 그래서 처음에는 관심을 거의 받지 못했다(little concern). 따라서 '전례 없는'이라는 뜻의 unprecedented는 문맥에 맞지 않으며, familiar(익숙한)나 unsurprising(놀랍지 않은)으로 고쳐야 한다.

body:
다음 문장과 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?

The 1969 fire was extinguished so quickly that nobody took a photograph of it.
solution: 「so ~ that …」은 '너무 ~해서 …하다'라는 뜻이다. 주어진 문장은 화재가 너무 빨리 진압되어 아무도 사진을 찍지 못했다는 의미이다. 이를 '누구도 사진을 찍기 전에 화재가 끝났다'로 바꾼 ②가 같은 의미이다. ①은 반대 의미이고, ③은 사진이 없었던 이유를 잘못 제시했다.
choices: The fire continued long enough for many people to photograph it.
The fire ended before anyone was able to photograph it.
Nobody photographed the fire because its cause was unknown.
The photograph in Time showed the fire immediately after it began.
Taking photographs helped firefighters extinguish the fire quickly.

body:
다음 글의 밑줄 친 (A)~(C)를 <조건>에 맞게 고쳐 쓰시오.

The Time article featured a photograph (A)taking several years earlier. It showed a fire that (B)has occurred before the 1969 fire, because the 1969 fire (C)put out too quickly for anyone to photograph it.

<조건>
· (A)는 한 단어로 쓸 것
· (B)는 1969년 화재보다 먼저 일어난 일임이 드러나는 시제로 쓸 것
· (C)는 밑줄 친 부분 전체(put out)를 고쳐 쓸 것
answer: (A) taken (B) had occurred (C) was put out
solution: (A) 사진은 '찍힌' 대상이므로 photograph를 뒤에서 수식하는 과거분사 taken이 알맞다. (B) 기준 시점인 1969년 화재(과거)보다 먼저 일어난 일이므로, 조건에 따라 과거완료 had occurred로 쓴다. (C) 화재는 '진압된' 대상이므로 수동태가 필요하다. 주어가 단수이고 시제가 과거이므로 was put out으로 쓴다.

body:
빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.

I completed the assignment, and my classmates ______, too.
solution: 빈칸은 앞의 동사구 completed the assignment를 대신해야 한다. 과거의 일반동사를 대신하는 대동사 did가 알맞다.

body:
빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.

Trying unfamiliar things was ______ for all of us.
solution: 주어 Trying unfamiliar things가 사람에게 흥미를 주는 것이므로 능동의 의미를 나타내는 exciting이 필요하다. excited는 감정을 느끼는 사람을 설명할 때 쓴다.

body: 다음 중 어법상 옳지 않은 것을 고르시오.
solution: discover의 목적어인 what절은 간접의문문이므로 평서문의 어순을 써야 한다. what were we good at은 what we were good at으로 고쳐야 한다.
choices: One classmate tried new foods, while another joined a writing club.
I learned from the experience, and my classmates did so, too.
The assignment helped us discover what were we good at.
There are many challenges that we can set for ourselves.
It is exciting to gain a different perspective on life.

body:
다음 글의 빈칸 (A)~(C)에 들어갈 말이 바르게 짝지어진 것을 고르시오.

I enjoyed the assignment, and my classmates (A) ______, too. Sharing our experiences was (B) ______. It also showed us what (C) ______ discover about ourselves.
solution: (A)에는 enjoyed the assignment를 대신하는 did가 필요하다. 경험을 공유하는 일이 흥미를 주므로 (B)는 exciting이고, 간접의문문의 어순에 따라 (C)는 we could가 알맞다.

body:
다음 글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중 어법상 옳지 않은 것만을 모두 고른 것은?

ⓐOne classmate tried new foods, while another joined a writing club. I enjoyed hearing about their experiences, and ⓑmy classmates were, too. ⓒIt was excited to share different perspectives. We then discussed ⓓchallenges that we could set for ourselves and wondered ⓔwhat could we discover through them.
solution: ⓑ의 were는 enjoyed hearing about their experiences를 대신하는 did로 고쳐야 한다. ⓒ는 사물이 주는 감정을 나타내므로 exciting이 알맞고, ⓔ는 간접의문문이므로 what we could discover가 되어야 한다.

body:
다음 우리말과 일치하도록 <보기>의 어구를 배열하여 문장을 완성하시오.

공장주들은 아이들에게 성인 노동자들보다 더 적은 돈을 지급할 수 있었다.

<보기>
children / could pay / than adult workers / factory owners / less

조건: 모든 어구를 한 번씩 사용하고, Factory owners로 시작할 것.
answer: Factory owners could pay children less than adult workers.
solution: ‘~에게 더 적은 돈을 지급하다’는 pay ~ less로 표현한다. 비교 대상인 adult workers 앞에 than을 놓아 문장을 완성한다.

body:
다음 우리말과 일치하도록 <보기>의 어구를 배열하여 문장을 완성하시오.

하인은 공장에 들어가기 위해 다른 직업을 가진 척했다.

<보기>
to enter factories / pretended / Hine / other jobs / to have

조건: 모든 어구를 한 번씩 사용하고, Hine으로 시작할 것.
answer: Hine pretended to have other jobs to enter factories.
solution: ‘~하는 척하다’는 pretend to부정사로 표현하므로 pretended 뒤에 to have other jobs를 놓는다. 공장에 들어가려는 목적은 to enter factories로 나타낸다.

body:
다음 우리말과 일치하도록 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞게 변형하여 빈칸에 한 단어를 쓰시오.

하인은 공장에서 일하고 있는 아이들의 사진을 찍었다.

Hine took photographs of children __________ in factories. (work)
solution: children과 work의 관계가 능동이므로 현재분사 working을 쓴다. working in factories가 앞의 children을 뒤에서 수식한다.

body:
다음 우리말과 일치하도록 <보기>의 어구를 배열하여 문장을 완성하시오.

사람들은 아이들의 기쁨 없는 표정을 보고 마음 아파하지 않을 수 없었다.

<보기>
when they saw / could not help / the children's joyless expressions / people / feeling heartbroken

조건: 모든 어구를 한 번씩 사용하고, People로 시작할 것.
answer: People could not help feeling heartbroken when they saw the children's joyless expressions.
solution: ‘~하지 않을 수 없다’는 cannot help -ing로 표현하므로 could not help 뒤에 feeling heartbroken을 놓는다. 사람들이 그러한 감정을 느낀 때를 나타내는 when절을 뒤에 연결한다.

body:
다음 우리말과 일치하도록 <보기>의 어구를 배열하여 문장을 완성하시오.

하인은 아이들의 노동 조건이 얼마나 위험한지를 보여 주고 싶어 했다.

<보기>
how dangerous / wanted to show / were / Hine / the children's working conditions

조건: 모든 어구를 한 번씩 사용하고, Hine으로 시작할 것.
answer: Hine wanted to show how dangerous the children's working conditions were.
solution: ‘얼마나 위험한지’는 how dangerous로 표현한다. show의 목적어로 쓰인 간접의문문에서는 how dangerous 뒤에 주어와 동사를 차례로 놓는다.

body:
다음 글의 내용을 요약한 문장의 빈칸 (1), (2)에 들어갈 말을 <보기>에서 골라 각각 한 단어로 쓰시오. 필요한 경우 어형을 바꾸시오.

Hine collected information about children in factories and photographed them. His pictures were presented to the public, helping people understand the seriousness of child labor.

요약문: Hine used photographs to draw public (1)__________ to the (2)__________ of child labor.

<보기>
serious / attention / ignore / comfort
solution: draw attention to는 '~에 관심을 끌다'라는 뜻이므로 (1)에는 attention이 들어간다. ignore를 명사형 ignorance로 바꾸어도 draw와 어울리지 않고, 사진을 공개한 목적과도 반대된다. (2)는 관사 the 뒤에서 of child labor의 수식을 받는 명사 자리이다. 본문의 'the seriousness of child labor'에 따라 serious를 seriousness로 바꾼다. comfort는 명사로 쓸 수 있지만 '아동 노동의 편안함'이 되어 글 내용과 맞지 않는다.

body:
다음 우리말과 일치하도록 <보기>의 어구를 배열하여 문장을 완성하시오.

1938년에 통과된 법은 열여섯 살 미만의 아이들이 수업 시간 중에 공장에서 일하는 것을 불법으로 만들었다.

<보기>
for children under sixteen / made it illegal / to work in factories / the act passed in 1938 / during school hours

조건: 모든 어구를 한 번씩 사용하고, The act로 시작할 것.
answer: The act passed in 1938 made it illegal for children under sixteen to work in factories during school hours.
solution: passed in 1938은 수동의 의미를 나타내는 과거분사구로, 앞의 the act를 수식한다. 'make it+형용사+for+의미상 주어+to부정사' 구문에서 it은 가목적어이고 to work in factories가 진목적어이다. for children under sixteen은 to부정사의 의미상 주어이므로 to work 바로 앞에 놓는다. 시간을 나타내는 부사구 during school hours는 문장 끝에 둔다.

body:
다음 우리말을 <조건>에 맞게 영작하시오.

공장주들에게 착취당하고 있던 아이들은 하인의 사진에 담겼다.

<조건>
• The children으로 시작할 것.
• take advantage of와 photograph를 각각 한 번씩 사용하되, 필요한 경우 어형을 바꿀 것.
• 아이들을 수식하는 절은 who로 시작하는 과거진행 수동태로 쓸 것.
• 주절은 과거시제 수동태로 쓰고, by Hine으로 끝낼 것.
answer: The children who were being taken advantage of by factory owners were photographed by Hine.
solution: take advantage of를 수동태로 바꾸어도 전치사 of는 남겨야 하므로 were being taken advantage of로 쓴다. 주절에서는 아이들이 촬영의 대상이므로 were photographed를 사용한다.

body:
다음 우리말과 일치하도록 <보기>의 어구를 배열하여 문장을 완성하시오.

공장주들은 여러 가지 이유로 아동 노동에 의존했다.

<보기>
for / turned / factory owners / child labor / several reasons / to

조건: 모든 어구를 한 번씩 사용하고, Factory owners로 시작할 것.
answer: Factory owners turned to child labor for several reasons.
solution: '~에 의존하다'는 turn to로 표현하므로 turned 바로 뒤에 to를 놓고, 그 목적어로 child labor를 쓴다. '여러 가지 이유로'는 전치사구 for several reasons로 나타내어 문장 끝에 둔다.

body:
다음 글의 내용을 한 문단으로 요약할 때, 빈칸 (1)~(3)에 들어갈 알맞은 말을 <보기>에서 골라 각각 한 단어로 쓰시오. (필요한 경우 어형을 바꿀 것)

Lewis Hine was a photographer who wanted to show the harsh reality of child labor. Since factory owners did not want outsiders to see their young workers, he often pretended to be a fire inspector or a salesman to get inside. His photographs shocked many Americans and made them aware of the problem. Thanks to the public's concern, many states passed stronger laws against child labor.

요약문: Lewis Hine worked in secret to (1)__________ the cruelty of child labor. His powerful photographs (2)__________ public awareness, and as a result many states (3)__________ stronger laws to stop it.

<보기> expose, conceal, raise, justify, pass, permit, ban
solution: (1) 하인은 아동 노동의 가혹한 현실을 보여 주려고 했으므로 '드러내다'라는 뜻의 expose가 알맞다. 반대 의미인 conceal과 '정당화하다'라는 뜻의 justify는 글 내용과 반대된다. to부정사 뒤이므로 원형 그대로 쓴다. (2) 본문의 'made them aware of the problem'은 '대중의 인식을 높였다'라는 뜻이다. 과거의 일이므로 raise를 과거형 raised로 쓴다. (3) 본문의 'many states passed stronger laws'에 따라 pass를 과거형 passed로 쓴다. permit과 ban은 laws를 목적어로 취하면 의미가 통하지 않는다.
